Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

This page uses EGNO's convention: the word "left" refers to the side on which
the dual object sits in the evaluation map.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear category
([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Since composition in
$\mathcal C$ is $k$-bilinear, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a
$k$-algebra with unit $\operatorname{id}_X$ for every object $X$.

An object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ is **absolutely simple** when the $k$-algebra
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is one-dimensional over $k$, that is,

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad \operatorname{id}_X\ne0 .$$

Equivalently, the evaluation map

$$k\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto\lambda\operatorname{id}_X ,$$

is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. These two formulations agree: the evaluation
map is $k$-linear and multiplicative with $1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_X$, and it
is injective because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X=0$ with $\operatorname{id}_X\ne0$ forces
$\lambda=0$; surjectivity is exactly
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$. In particular a
nonzero endomorphism space $k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$ has dimension one, so an
absolutely simple object is not a zero object; if $\mathcal C$ has a zero object
then $X\ne0$ automatically.

In a $k$-linear abelian category, a simple object with
$\operatorname{End}(X)=k$ satisfies this condition ([[def-simple-object]]).
The converse need not hold: the representation $k\xrightarrow{1}k$ of the
two-vertex quiver has only scalar endomorphisms but has the proper nonzero
subrepresentation $0\to k$. Thus the definition records the scalar
endomorphism condition without asserting simplicity in an arbitrary abelian
category.
Every simple object of a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category over an
algebraically closed field $k$ is absolutely simple. Indeed, a nonzero
endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is
an isomorphism; its endomorphism algebra $D$ is therefore a division algebra.
Local finiteness makes $D$ finite-dimensional
([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]). For $a\in D$, a polynomial
over $k$ annihilates $a$ by linear dependence of its powers; it splits into
linear factors, and a division algebra has no zero divisors, so one factor
$a-\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ vanishes. Thus $D=k$. This definition
fixes no semisimplicity and no algebraic-closedness hypothesis; it records them
only as the standard situation in which absolute simplicity is automatic.

If $X$ is absolutely simple, every automorphism of $X$ is a scalar
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\in k^{\times}$: it is an invertible
endomorphism, hence by absolute simplicity equals some
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\lambda$ is invertible with inverse
$\lambda^{-1}$ because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ is invertible.

Let $A$ be indeterminate, $F=\mathbb Q(A)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the concrete module, finite $R$ series, duality, pivotal comparison $G_N$, and twist $\lambda_N$ in the normalized colored Jones definition are admissible ribbon data. More precisely, take the $F$-linear category generated by all those modules under finite tensor products, chosen contragredient duals, finite direct sums, and images of module-idempotents, with all module maps as morphisms. Its braiding on weight vectors is the finite series
$$R_{X,Y}=D_{X,Y}\sum_{r\ge0}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}E_X^r\otimes F_Y^r,\qquad D_{X,Y}(x_h\otimes y_k)=A^{hk}x_h\otimes y_k.$$
The sum is finite on each pair. Its pivotal comparison on weight $h$ is $(-1)^h q_K^h$, and its twist on $V_N$ is $(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}I$. These give natural invertible braidings with both hexagons, both duality snakes, the balancing identity and dual compatibility of twist. In particular all colors $N$, rather than a fixed bounded range of colors, are covered.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every integer $N\ge1$ and every finite braid word $\beta$ on $b\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the normalized generic quotient
$$\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes b}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}$$
belongs to $\mathbb Z[A^4,A^{-4}]$. Consequently there is a unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ whose substitution $q=A^4$ equals that quotient. It is independent of the braid representative, has $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, and agrees with the normalized colored Jones convention of Murakami’s explicit matrix definition in the variable $q$. Its value at every nonzero complex $q$, in particular $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$, means evaluation of this Laurent polynomial; it never means division by the specialized quantum dimension.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The diagonal weights give $K_L E K_L^{-1}v_j=q_L^2Ev_j$ and $K_L F K_L^{-1}v_j=q_L^{-2}Fv_j$. For the commutator, $EFv_j-FEv_j=([j+1][N-j-1]-[N-j][j])v_j=[N-1-2j]v_j$; the last equality follows by expanding the two quantum-number products over $q_K-q_K^{-1}$. Since $[r]_{q_K}=[r]_{q_L}$, this is $(K_L-K_L^{-1})(q_L-q_L^{-1})^{-1}v_j$. The generators therefore satisfy the defining $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations.

The eigenvalues $q_L^{N-1-2j}$ of $K_L$ are pairwise distinct in $F$. Any module endomorphism is therefore diagonal in the given basis; commuting with $E$, whose successive coefficients $[N-j]$ are nonzero in $F$, forces all diagonal entries to be equal. Thus $\operatorname{End}_{U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)}(V_N)=F I$ and the color is absolutely simple by [F6].

If $N=1$, $V_N$ is one-dimensional and irreducible. For $N>1$, let $W$ be a nonzero submodule and choose $x=\sum_j c_jv_j\in W$ nonzero. The eigenvalues of $K_L$ are distinct, so the polynomial spectral projection for any $j$ with $c_j\ne0$ maps $x$ to $c_jv_j$; hence $v_j\in W$. Repeated application of $E$ gives $v_0\in W$, since every coefficient $[N-k]$ encountered is nonzero. Repeated application of $F$ to $v_0$ gives each $v_k$ because the coefficients $[k]$ are nonzero. Thus $W=V_N$, proving irreducibility.

The displayed sum for $d_N$ is a geometric sum, so $d_N=(-1)^{N-1}[N]$. Its numerator $A^{2N}-A^{-2N}$ is a nonzero Laurent polynomial and its denominator $A^2-A^{-2}$ is nonzero in $F$; hence the generic normalization is defined. The Hopf coproduct [F2] supplies the tensor-power action used in $\rho_N(\beta)$. By the braiding, dual, and ribbon axioms [F3] and the all-color ribbon identities [F7], these matrices define the framed evaluation, whose value is the pivotal trace by [F5].

By [F4], [F7], and [A2], $\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}t_N(\beta)$ is unchanged by every conjugation and Markov stabilization, since $V_N$ is absolutely simple and its specified twist scalar is nonzero. Countable choice [A3] supplies the evaluator's hypothesis. Dividing by the fixed nonzero $d_N$ preserves that equality, so the displayed generic value is independent of the braid representative.

The unknot is represented by the one-strand identity braid, whose exponent sum is zero and whose pivotal trace is $\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=d_N$. Hence $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\bigcirc;q)=1$. For $N\ge2$, at $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$ choose $A_N=e^{\pi i/(2N)}$; then $A_N^4=q_N$ and $A_N^2-A_N^{-2}\ne0$, while $A_N^{2N}-A_N^{-2N}=e^{\pi i}-e^{-\pi i}=0$. Thus $d_N(q_N)=0$: the generic quotient cannot be evaluated there by dividing by $d_N$.

Apply [F8] to the given knot-closing braid and color under [A2] and [A3]. The generic quotient therefore has a unique integral Laurent representative in $q=A^4$. Substitution into that finite Laurent sum is defined for every nonzero complex $q$, including $q_N$; it does not divide by the specialized quantum dimension. Together with steps 2.1 and 2.2, this proves the stated representative independence, unknot normalization and root-evaluation convention.

Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$
Use the contragredient left-dual action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ on $V_N^*$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(f\otimes v)=f(v)$ and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v_j\otimes v_j^*$. The ambient category is the $F$-linear category generated by the modules $V_N$ for all $N\ge1$ under finite tensor products, contragredient duals, finite direct sums and images of module-idempotents, whose morphisms are module homomorphisms, and whose tensor-product action is induced by the stated Hopf coproduct; its tensor unit is $F$ with the trivial action, so its tensor-unit endomorphism ring is $F$. These matrix data satisfy the ribbon-category axioms: braiding and inverse braiding, both duality snakes, monoidal pivotal comparison, balancing and dual compatibility of twist. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the framed-tangle and Markov constructions. An oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ presented as the closure of an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ has generic normalized value
$$J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}\in F,$$
where, for a word $\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, $w(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$, and $\rho_N(\beta)$ is obtained by replacing each positive braid generator by $c_N$ on the corresponding adjacent tensor factors and each inverse generator by $c_N^{-1}$, then composing in word order. This quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial in $A^4$. Define the **normalized colored Jones sequence** by the unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ satisfying $J_N(K;A^4)=J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;A^4)$. Its root value $J_N(K;q_N)$ is obtained by substituting into this Laurent polynomial. The variable transport to the ordinary Jones convention is $t=q^{-1}=A^{-4}$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $q_K=A^2$, $q_L=A^{-2}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Use the fundamental module, positive crossing, duality maps, and twist fixed in the preceding definition. For every $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the categorical ribbon trace of its blackboard-framed closure and let $w(\beta)$ be its exponent sum. With $t=A^{-4}$ and $z_0=-1/(t+1)$, the exact identities are
$$t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle=\delta^n(-A)^{w(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\ z=z_0},$$
$$(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)=\delta(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}\langle\widehat\beta\rangle.$$
Here $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is the normalized type-A Hecke Markov trace with braid generator sent to $T_i$, and $\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$ is the Kauffman bracket in the fixed crossing chart. The second identity is a value-by-value normalization formula; it does not by itself assert a Jones-polynomial specialization.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ and $t$ be formal variables and $K$ a
nonempty oriented link. At each crossing of a regular diagram $D$ use the
source chart with over-strand southwest-to-northeast: A joins left and right
endpoints with coefficient $A$, and B joins top and bottom endpoints with
coefficient $A^{-1}$. A state $S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$ assigns one smoothing at every
crossing; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count these choices and $|S|$ count the
resulting circles. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection
plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the
ambient oriented $3$-sphere. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under}), \qquad \operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c),$$
$$f_K(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)} \sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}.$$
For an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ whose oriented closure is $K$, let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$, where $\sigma_i$
is the positive geometric Artin half twist. Let $H(n)$ be the type-A Hecke
algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation $T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid
relations, and distant commutation, and let $\pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i$. Its
normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$ satisfies
$\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Define the library
Jones value by
$$V_K(t)=s^{e(\beta)}\left(-\frac{s^2+1}{s}\right)^{n-1} \operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\Big|_{v=s^2,\,z=-1/(s^2+1),\,t=s^2},$$
where $s=t^{1/2}$. With $A=t^{-1/4}$, these values satisfy
$$V_K(t)=f_K(t^{-1/4}).$$

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Assume AC. For every $n\ge1$ the published surjection
$\varphi_n\colon B_n^{\mathrm{Artin}}\to B_n^{\mathrm{geom}}$ of
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] is an
isomorphism. Equivalently, every word in
$\sigma_1^{\pm1},\dots,\sigma_{n-1}^{\pm1}$ whose geometric braid is trivial is
equivalent to the empty word using only the two Artin relations and free
insertions and deletions of adjacent inverse pairs, so that the Artin
presentation of [[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]] is a presentation
of the geometric braid group.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $Q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)$ be the base configuration of
[[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]], with $h=\frac{1}{4(n+1)}$ and
$q_j=((2j-n-1)h,0)$. Fix an index $i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$. The two adjacent
base points are

$$q_i=\bigl((2i-n-1)h,0\bigr),\qquad q_{i+1}=\bigl((2i+1-n)h,0\bigr),$$

their **midpoint** is $m_i:=(q_i+q_{i+1})/2=((2i-n)h,0)=q_i+(h,0)$, and their
**support disc** is the open disc

$$U_i:=\bigl\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\lVert w-m_i\rVert_2<\tfrac32h\bigr\}.$$

The support disc contains the two base points $q_i,q_{i+1}$, whose distance from
$m_i$ is $h$, and it contains no other base point: for $k<i$ one has
$\lVert q_k-m_i\rVert_2=(2(i-k)+1)h\ge 3h$ and for $k>i+1$ one has
$\lVert q_k-m_i\rVert_2=(2(k-i)-1)h\ge3h$, both exceeding $\tfrac32h$. Moreover
$U_i\subseteq D^\circ$, because every point of $U_i$ has norm at most
$\lVert m_i\rVert_2+\tfrac32h\le(n-2)h+\tfrac32h<(n+1)h<1$. Finally
$U_i\cap U_j=\varnothing$ whenever $|i-j|>1$, since then the midpoints are at
distance $2|i-j|h\ge4h>3h$, twice the radius.

**The positive half twist.** Define $\rho\colon I\to\mathbb R^2$, the
**anticlockwise diamond path**, by

$$\rho(t):=\begin{cases}\bigl(2th-h,\,-2th\bigr),&0\le t\le \tfrac12,\\[2pt] \bigl(2th-h,\,2th-2h\bigr),&\tfrac12\le t\le1.\end{cases}$$

Thus $\rho(0)=(-h,0)$, $\rho(\tfrac12)=(0,-h)$, $\rho(1)=(h,0)$, and $\rho$ is
continuous, piecewise linear, and satisfies $\lVert\rho(t)\rVert_2\le h$ for all
$t$ with $\rho(t)\neq0$ throughout. The **elementary half twist at $i$**, written
$\sigma_i$, is the tuple of motions

$$(\sigma_i)_i(t):=m_i+\rho(t),\qquad (\sigma_i)_{i+1}(t):=m_i-\rho(t),\qquad (\sigma_i)_k(t):=q_k\ \ (k\notin\{i,i+1\}).$$

It is a braid based at $Q$
([[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]],
[[def-continuous-map-top]]): the two moving points stay in $U_i$ and are
antipodal about $m_i$, so they are distinct; every other point is fixed and lies
outside $U_i$; and the endpoint permutation is the transposition of $i$ and
$i+1$, since $(\sigma_i)_i(1)=m_i+(h,0)=q_{i+1}$ and
$(\sigma_i)_{i+1}(1)=m_i-(h,0)=q_i$.

The words *positive* and *anticlockwise* refer to the fixed orientation of the
plane of the disc and to the fixed planar projection whose horizontal axis
contains $Q$: the moving pair turns through the half turn anticlockwise, the
label $i$ passing below its midpoint and the label $i+1$ above. Together with
the first-under-second stacking convention of
[[prop-stacking-of-geometric-braids-is-well-defined]] this fixes the sign
convention for every signed crossing on this page and its companion.

**The opposite half twist.** The **opposite** (clockwise) half twist at $i$ is
defined by the reflected path

$$\rho^{-}(t):=\bigl(\rho_1(t),-\rho_2(t)\bigr),$$

through the motions $(\sigma_i^{-})_i(t):=m_i+\rho^{-}(t)$,
$(\sigma_i^{-})_{i+1}(t):=m_i-\rho^{-}(t)$ and
$(\sigma_i^{-})_k(t):=q_k$ for $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$. It is again a braid supported
in $U_i$ with endpoint permutation the transposition of $i$ and $i+1$; its pair
turns through the same half turn clockwise, the label $i$ passing above the
midpoint. The two motions are not equal, and they are not related by a
reparametrisation of the height: they are the two signed crossings of the pair.

**The opposite motion is the group inverse.** For a braid $\beta$ the reversed
braid $\overline\beta_j(t)=z_{\pi(\beta)^{-1}(j)}(1-t)$ represents
$[\beta]^{-1}$ in the group $G_n$
([[thm-geometric-braids-form-a-group]]). For $\beta=\sigma_i$ one computes
$\overline{\sigma_i}=\sigma_i^{-}$: reversing the height and relabelling by the
transposition of $i$ and $i+1$ sends $\rho(t)=m_i+(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ to the
motion with relative path $-\rho(1-t)$, which is the reflected path
$\rho^-$ traversed from $t=0$ to $t=1$. Hence

$$[\sigma_i^{-}]=[\sigma_i]^{-1}\qquad\text{in }G_n .$$

**Elementary cases.** For $n\le1$ there is no index $i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$,
and there are no elementary half twists; the assertions above are vacuous. For
$n\ge2$ and $1\le i\le n-1$ both $[\sigma_i]$ and $[\sigma_i^{-}]$ are
nonidentity elements of $G_n$, since their endpoint permutations are
transpositions, which are not the identity permutation.

**Two letters do not commute in general.** For adjacent indices the supports
$U_i$ and $U_{i+1}$ overlap and no commutation is asserted;
[[lem-geometric-far-commutativity]] proves commutativity only for disjoint
supports.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every oriented link $L\subset\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$
is equivalent to the oriented closure $\widehat\beta$ of a geometric braid
$\beta$ on some number $n\ge0$ of strands, with $n\ge1$ when $L$ is nonempty.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For $N=1$, the basis has one vector, $E=F=0$, $K_L=1$, $c_1=G_1=1$, $d_1=\lambda_1=1$. Every braid generator therefore acts as $1$, and the normalized value of every such knot closure is $1$. For the unknot at any $N$, the one-strand identity braid has $w=0$ and trace $\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=d_N$, so its normalized value is also $1$.

The strand permutation of $\sigma_1^3$ is $(12)^3=(12)$, so its two endpoints are interchanged; pairing each bottom endpoint with the top endpoint in the same position therefore produces one component. At $N=2$, the only nonzero terms of $\mathcal R_2$ are $r=0,1$. On the ordered basis $(v_+v_+,v_+v_-,v_-v_+,v_-v_-)$ they give $c_2=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}$ and $G_2\otimes G_2=\operatorname{diag}(A^4,1,1,A^{-4})$. The middle block $B=\begin{pmatrix}0&A^{-1}\\A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}\end{pmatrix}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(B^3)=A^3-A^{-9}$ by direct multiplication; the other two diagonal entries of $c_2^3$ are $A^3$, hence $\operatorname{Tr}((G_2\otimes G_2)c_2^3)=A^7+A^3+A^{-1}-A^{-9}$. Here $w(\sigma_1^3)=3$, $\lambda_2=-A^3$, and $d_2=-A^2-A^{-2}$.

Write a braid word as $\beta=\prod_{j=1}^m\sigma_{i_j}^{\varepsilon_j}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, using [F4] under [A1]. Each letter gives one crossing in the braid box. The closure pairs endpoints as prescribed by [F5]; in the diagram convention fixed in the Example, the joining arcs are routed outside the rectangular braid box without added crossings. A positive letter contributes $+1$ to writhe by [F6]. For a negative letter the opposite half twist [F7] exchanges the over- and under-strands; the determinant in the crossing-sign definition changes sign when its two vectors are exchanged, so that crossing contributes $-1$. Thus $\operatorname{wr}(\widehat\beta)=\sum_j\varepsilon_j=w(\beta)$ by [F8].
Substitution into [F1] using step 1.2 yields $J_2^{\mathrm{gen}}(T;q)=\frac{A^{-9}(A^7+A^3+A^{-1}-A^{-9})}{A^2+A^{-2}}=A^{-4}+A^{-12}-A^{-16}=t+t^3-t^4$, where $t=A^{-4}=q^{-1}$.

Given an oriented knot $K\subset\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$, choose a braid closure $\widehat\beta$ representing it by [F9]. By [F2], the fundamental-color ribbon trace is $\delta$ times the raw bracket and the twist is $-A^3$. Since $d_2=\delta$, formula [F1] gives $J_2^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$. By step 1.3 this is the writhe-normalized bracket $f_K(A)$. The use of [F9] requires [A1], and the framed trace in [F2] requires [A2].

The bracket/Jones theorem [F3] now gives $f_K(A)=V_K(t)$ at $t=A^{-4}=q^{-1}$. Its hypothesis uses AC [A1], while the ribbon-trace identification in [F2] uses ACω [A2], already supplied in step 2.2; the proof keeps those axiom branches separate. Therefore $J_2^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=V_K(q^{-1})$.

citations.quote: For every valid input of the colored-braid evaluation algorithm, where the braid word has $m$ letters and the total tensor-product dimension is $D$, the procedure terminates after exactly $m$ crossing-matrix updates and one finite pivotal-trace contraction. It returns the ribbon-category evaluation of that framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. The stated bound concerns the number of matrix updates; each update is a finite exact matrix multiplication over the effective field.

Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

This page uses EGNO's convention: the word "left" refers to the side on which
the dual object sits in the evaluation map.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Upon each sufficiently large specialization in step 2.1 it is precisely [F2]'s ribbon twist, so the equation holds by the same infinite-root argument as step 3.1. On $V_N$, its specialized matrix is $s_\ell^{(N-1)(N+1)}I$ by [F2]; infinite-root interpolation therefore gives $\theta^+_{V_N}=A^{N^2-1}I$ generically. On a weight-$h$ vector define $p_X=(-1)^h$. This is a module map because $E,F$ change weight by $2$; it is natural because module maps preserve weights, monoidal because weights add, and involutive. On dual weights $-h$ it satisfies $p_{X^*}=(p_X)^*$, and $p$ commutes with the braiding. Set $j=pj^+$ and $\theta=p\theta^+$. Substitution into the unsigned balancing and dual-compatibility equations proves the corresponding equations for $\theta$; monoidality of $p$ proves that $j$ is a pivotal comparison. Let $A$ be an indeterminate, put $q=A^4$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}=q_K^{-1}$, and work over $F=\mathbb Q(A)$. An oriented knot in $S^3$ means a smooth embedded circle with an orientation, considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy. For an integer $r$, put
$$[r]=\frac{q_K^r-q_K^{-r}}{q_K-q_K^{-1}},\qquad [m]!=\prod_{r=1}^{m}[r]\quad(m\ge1),\qquad [0]!=1.$$
For each $N\ge1$, put $q_N=\exp(2\pi i/N)$.
For each integer $N\ge1$, let $V_N$ have basis $v_0,\ldots,v_{N-1}$ and define the $U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ action in the library coproduct convention by
$$K_Lv_j=q_L^{N-1-2j}v_j,\qquad Ev_j=[N-j]v_{j-1},\qquad Fv_j=[j+1]v_{j+1},$$
where $v_{-1}=v_N=0$. In the universal $R$-matrix formula use $q_K$ and $H v_j=(N-1-2j)v_j$; on $V_N\otimes V_N$ its action is the finite sum
$$\mathcal R_N=q_K^{H\otimes H/2}\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}\,E^r\otimes F^r,$$
and the positive crossing is $c_N=P\mathcal R_N$, where $P(x\otimes y)=y\otimes x$. This is an irreducible module of dimension $N$. Equip these matrices with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon data: the twist matrix is the scalar $\theta_N=\lambda_N I$ with $\lambda_N=(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}$, and the matrix $G_N=(-1)^{N-1}\operatorname{diag}(A^{2(N-1-2j)})_{j=0}^{N-1}$ is the pivotal comparison used in the closure trace. The resulting generic quantum dimension is
$$d_N=\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=(-1)^{N-1}\frac{A^{2N}-A^{-2N}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$
Use the contragredient left-dual action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ on $V_N^*$, with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(f\otimes v)=f(v)$ and coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}v_j\otimes v_j^*$. The ambient category is the $F$-linear category generated by the modules $V_N$ for all $N\ge1$ under finite tensor products, contragredient duals, finite direct sums and images of module-idempotents, whose morphisms are module homomorphisms, and whose tensor-product action is induced by the stated Hopf coproduct; its tensor unit is $F$ with the trivial action, so its tensor-unit endomorphism ring is $F$. These matrix data satisfy the ribbon-category axioms: braiding and inverse braiding, both duality snakes, monoidal pivotal comparison, balancing and dual compatibility of twist. Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice for the framed-tangle and Markov constructions. An oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ presented as the closure of an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ has generic normalized value
$$J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;q)=\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes n}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}\in F,$$
where, for a word $\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_m}^{\varepsilon_m}$ with $\varepsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}$, $w(\beta):=\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j$, and $\rho_N(\beta)$ is obtained by replacing each positive braid generator by $c_N$ on the corresponding adjacent tensor factors and each inverse generator by $c_N^{-1}$, then composing in word order. This quotient is an integral Laurent polynomial in $A^4$. Define the **normalized colored Jones sequence** by the unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ satisfying $J_N(K;A^4)=J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(K;A^4)$. Its root value $J_N(K;q_N)$ is obtained by substituting into this Laurent polynomial. The variable transport to the ordinary Jones convention is $t=q^{-1}=A^{-4}$.

Let $A$ be indeterminate, $F=\mathbb Q(A)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the concrete module, finite $R$ series, duality, pivotal comparison $G_N$, and twist $\lambda_N$ in the normalized colored Jones definition are admissible ribbon data. More precisely, take the $F$-linear category generated by all those modules under finite tensor products, chosen contragredient duals, finite direct sums, and images of module-idempotents, with all module maps as morphisms. Its braiding on weight vectors is the finite series
$$R_{X,Y}=D_{X,Y}\sum_{r\ge0}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}E_X^r\otimes F_Y^r,\qquad D_{X,Y}(x_h\otimes y_k)=A^{hk}x_h\otimes y_k.$$
The sum is finite on each pair. Its pivotal comparison on weight $h$ is $(-1)^h q_K^h$, and its twist on $V_N$ is $(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}I$. These give natural invertible braidings with both hexagons, both duality snakes, the balancing identity and dual compatibility of twist. In particular all colors $N$, rather than a fixed bounded range of colors, are covered.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category with chosen left duals and twist
$\theta$ ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), let $X\in\mathcal C$, let
$n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, and let $\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the
blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$: the closed framed tangle diagram obtained
from the $(n,n)$-tangle diagram of $\beta$ by joining its top boundary points
to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle
evaluation functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].
Consequently $t_n(\beta)$ depends only on the framed isotopy class of
$\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$, and the blackboard-framed closure of the positive
stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear category
([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Since composition in
$\mathcal C$ is $k$-bilinear, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a
$k$-algebra with unit $\operatorname{id}_X$ for every object $X$.

An object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ is **absolutely simple** when the $k$-algebra
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is one-dimensional over $k$, that is,

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad \operatorname{id}_X\ne0 .$$

Equivalently, the evaluation map

$$k\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto\lambda\operatorname{id}_X ,$$

is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. These two formulations agree: the evaluation
map is $k$-linear and multiplicative with $1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_X$, and it
is injective because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X=0$ with $\operatorname{id}_X\ne0$ forces
$\lambda=0$; surjectivity is exactly
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$. In particular a
nonzero endomorphism space $k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$ has dimension one, so an
absolutely simple object is not a zero object; if $\mathcal C$ has a zero object
then $X\ne0$ automatically.

In a $k$-linear abelian category, a simple object with
$\operatorname{End}(X)=k$ satisfies this condition ([[def-simple-object]]).
The converse need not hold: the representation $k\xrightarrow{1}k$ of the
two-vertex quiver has only scalar endomorphisms but has the proper nonzero
subrepresentation $0\to k$. Thus the definition records the scalar
endomorphism condition without asserting simplicity in an arbitrary abelian
category.
Every simple object of a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category over an
algebraically closed field $k$ is absolutely simple. Indeed, a nonzero
endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is
an isomorphism; its endomorphism algebra $D$ is therefore a division algebra.
Local finiteness makes $D$ finite-dimensional
([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]). For $a\in D$, a polynomial
over $k$ annihilates $a$ by linear dependence of its powers; it splits into
linear factors, and a division algebra has no zero divisors, so one factor
$a-\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ vanishes. Thus $D=k$. This definition
fixes no semisimplicity and no algebraic-closedness hypothesis; it records them
only as the standard situation in which absolute simplicity is automatic.

If $X$ is absolutely simple, every automorphism of $X$ is a scalar
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\in k^{\times}$: it is an invertible
endomorphism, hence by absolute simplicity equals some
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\lambda$ is invertible with inverse
$\lambda^{-1}$ because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ is invertible.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: On the displayed color basis, $E^r/[r]!$ sends $v_i$ to $\begin{bmatrix}a-i+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_{q_K}v_{i-r}$, with zero outside the index range, while $F^rv_j=\prod_{s=1}^r[j+s]v_{j+r}$. By [F2] each coefficient in the finite $R$ series therefore belongs to $R_0$, including the weight factor $A^{hk}$. Its inverse is $\bigl(\sum_{r\ge0}(-1)^rq_K^{-r(r-1)/2}z^rE^r\otimes F^r/[r]!\bigr)D^{-1}$, again a finite integral matrix by the same argument. To check the inverse formula, the coefficient of $(E\otimes F)^m$ in the product of the two nilpotent series is, after multiplication by $[m]!/z^m$, $\sum_{r=0}^m(-1)^{m-r}q_K^{r(r-1)/2-(m-r)(m-r-1)/2}\begin{bmatrix}m\\r\end{bmatrix}_{q_K}$. Its exponent equals $(m-1)r-m(m-1)/2$, so for $m>0$ it vanishes by [F2]'s alternating Gauss sum; at $m=0$ it is $1$. Thus both $c$ and $c^{-1}$ are integral matrices.

Ordinary dual evaluation and coevaluation have entries $0,1$. The pivotal matrices $G_N$ and $G_N^{-1}$ are diagonal Laurent monomials with signs. Accordingly both orientations of cup and cap are integral: one uses ordinary evaluation/coevaluation, the other their composites with the pivotal comparison or its inverse. Crossings involving a dual strand are obtained by bending one or both strands of $c$ or $c^{-1}$ with those maps, as follows from braiding naturality at evaluation and the snakes; concretely this is a partial transpose followed by the just-listed integral contractions. It introduces no matrix inverse other than $c^{-1}$ and $G_N^{-1}$. Every elementary matrix of a tangle colored by $V_N$ and its dual is thus over $R_0$.

It remains to prove the stronger exponent assertion. Work temporarily over $\mathbb Q(i)(A)$, and let a prime denote substitution $A\mapsto iA$. On the basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ put $Qv_j=(-1)^{j(j-1)/2}v_j$ and $Dv_j=(-1)^jv_j$. The $r$th term of $R$ sends input $(u,v)$ to $(u-r,v+r)$, before the flip. Every nonzero Laurent monomial in its coefficient has degree, modulo $4$, $ (a-2u)(a-2v)+2r(a-u+v+r)\equiv a^2-2a(u+v)+2r(a-u+v+r)\pmod4.$ Indeed $[m]$ has all degrees congruent to $2(m-1)$, $z$ has degree $2$, $q_K^{r(r-1)/2}$ has degree $r(r-1)$, and the weight factor is evaluated at the output weights. The quotient of the output and input $Q\otimes Q$ signs is $(-1)^{r(v-u+r)}$. Comparing these two explicit expressions yields $c'=(Q\otimes Q)c(Q\otimes Q)^{-1}\quad(a\text{ even}),$ $c'=i(Q\otimes Q)(D\otimes1)c(D\otimes1)(Q\otimes Q)^{-1}\quad(a\text{ odd}).$ For the second formula, the remaining sign is $(-1)^{u+v+r}$, exactly the product of the left input and left output $D$ signs after the flip. No asymptotic or numerical specialization is used in these matrix equalities.

Cut a small oriented arc of the framed knot closure of $\beta$. The remaining framed $(1,1)$-tangle is a morphism $f:V_N\to V_N$ (choose its endpoint orientation accordingly). A generic planar projection decomposes it into finitely many elementary crossings, cups and caps, so step 2.1 makes every entry of $f$ an element of $R_0$. By [F1] and [F3], $f=sI$ for a scalar $s\in F$; its $v_0$ diagonal entry gives $s\in R_0$. Closing that cut arc is the pivotal trace of $f$, namely $d_Ns$, and is the same framed knot value as $\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes b}\rho_N(\beta))$ by [F3]. Since $d_N\ne0$ generically, the quotient in the Statement is $\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}s\in R_0$. This proves integral Laurentness in $A$ without dividing in an integral ring or after specialization.

If $a$ is even, let $T=Q^{\otimes b}$. Step 2.2 gives $\rho'=T\rho T^{-1}$ for every braid word, including inverses. Direct substitution gives $G_N'=G_N$, $d_N'=d_N$ and $\lambda_N'=\lambda_N$, because $a$ and $a(a+2)$ are even and divisible by $4$, respectively. Since $T$ commutes with $G_N^{\otimes b}$, cyclicity of the ordinary trace shows that the normalized quotient is unchanged by $A\mapsto iA$.

If $a$ is odd, put $H=D^0\otimes D^1\otimes\cdots\otimes D^{b-1}$ and $T=Q^{\otimes b}H$. The operator $c$ preserves the sum of basis indices, so it commutes with $D\otimes D$. Consequently conjugating an adjacent $c$ by $H$ has the effect $(D\otimes1)c(D\otimes1)$, regardless of which adjacent position has odd exponent. Step 2.2 thus gives $\rho'=i^{w(\beta)}T\rho T^{-1}$. Here $G_N'=-G_N$, $d_N'=-d_N$, and $\lambda_N'=-i\lambda_N$, since $a(a+2)\equiv3\pmod4$. Taking the trace and normalizing therefore multiplies the quotient by $(-1)^{b-1+w(\beta)}$. The strand permutation of a knot-closing braid is a single $b$-cycle, so its sign is $(-1)^{b-1}$. Each positive or negative generator is a transposition, so that same sign is $(-1)^{w(\beta)}$. The multiplier is $1$. This proves invariance under $A\mapsto iA$ also for odd $a$.

Write the integral Laurent polynomial from step 3.1 as $\sum_k n_kA^k$, where $n_k\in\mathbb Z$ and only finitely many are nonzero. Steps 3.2 and 3.3 imply $\sum_kn_k(i^k-1)A^k=0$. Linear independence of Laurent monomials over $\mathbb Q(i)$ gives $n_k=0$ unless $4\mid k$. Replacing $A^{4m}$ by $q^m$ gives the required unique integral Laurent polynomial. Its representative independence and unknot value follow from [F1]. Evaluation of a finite Laurent sum at a nonzero complex number is defined without any denominator other than a power of that number, even when the generic quantum dimension specializes to zero. This proves every assertion, including the root-evaluation interpretation.

To check the conventional variable explicitly, write $a=N-1$ and $\{m\}=q^{m/2}-q^{-m/2}$, $\{m\}!=\prod_{s=1}^m\{s\}$. Murakami's defining positive matrix on basis $e_0,\ldots,e_a$ has coefficient, for input $(k,l)$ and output $(I,J)=(l-r,k+r)$, $\frac{\{l\}!\{a-k\}!}{\{l-r\}!\{r\}!\{a-k-r\}!}q^{(I-a/2)(J-a/2)-r(I-J)/2-r(r+1)/4},$ with $0\le r\le\min(l,a-k)$, and pivotal diagonal $\mu e_j=q^{(2j-a)/2}e_j$; these are the explicit defining formulas in §2.4, not an invoked invariance theorem. At $q=A^4$, change basis by $v_j=A^{j^2}([j]![a-j]!)^{-1}e_{a-j}$. For input $(u,v)$, reversal makes the output $(v+r,u-r)$. The factorial coefficient changes to $z^r[a-u+r]![v+r]!/([a-u]![v]![r]!)$, exactly the one in step 1.1. Before scaling, the exponent of $A$ differs from the declared $R$ coefficient by $2r(v-u+r)$; the change-of-basis factor $A^{u^2+v^2-(u-r)^2-(v+r)^2}$ is its inverse. Thus the two positive crossing matrices are conjugate, as are their inverses, and $\mu$ becomes $K=q_K^H$. Murakami's twist-normalizing scalar is $A^{a(a+2)}$. Replacing this unsigned pivotal and twist by the signed ones of our definition multiplies the normalized closed-braid quotient by $(-1)^{a(b-1-w(\beta))}=1$, by the knot-permutation parity proved in step 3.3. Consequently the Laurent polynomial just established is exactly that source's normalized colored Jones polynomial with $q=A^4$.
